title: Kitchener Legacy Walk and newcomer strategy approved
subtitle: Heritage designations, Digital Kitchener strategy, school-zone parking changes, active transportation route, water capacity update and Enova board appointments
overview: Council backed a new public art idea, the Kitchener Legacy Walk, directing staff to report on a path of murals from Victoria Park to Centre In The Square honouring locals with international achievements, aimed at a 2029 launch {{vote:m19}}. Budget details will come later through the arts action plan and a separate budget issue paper.

Council also approved the city's first Municipal Newcomer Strategy, with $25,000 a year for Immigration Partnership Waterloo Region {{vote:m16}}, and a refreshed Digital Kitchener strategy for 2026-2030 {{vote:m10}}. Several properties moved toward heritage designation, and the Active Transportation Route 2 work, new crossings and school-zone parking changes were approved. One Patricia Avenue parking proposal was deferred to June 29 for consultation {{vote:m12}}.

The Mayor gave an update on the regional water capacity constraint, saying the Region expects sustainable operations to be restored around 2027 and urging water conservation this spring and summer. Council also made Enova board appointments and ratified appeal committee decisions on two dog designations.

decisions.detail: Council directed staff to report on a phased public art walk from Victoria Park to Centre In The Square, with a launch tied to the city's 175th anniversary in 2029.
Council approved the city's first newcomer strategy and $25,000 in annual funding for Immigration Partnership Waterloo Region, with other costs referred to future budgets.
Council approved the refreshed strategy to guide digital initiatives, priorities and investments from 2026 to 2030.

Council removed the Prospect Avenue school bus loading zone, created one on Emerald Avenue, prohibited parking on part of St. Leger Street, and deferred the Patricia Avenue stopping restriction to June 29, 2026 for consultation.
Council approved wayfinding for the Stanley Park to Uptown Waterloo route, four pedestrian crossovers and neighbourhood bikeways on several streets.
Council agreed to pursue heritage designation for 265 Weber Street East, 141-149 Borden Avenue North and 55 King Street West.
Council appointed three councillors to the Enova boards from June 1, 2026, and three independent directors to Enova Energy Corporation.
Council approved a zoning by-law amendment for Blocks 1-3, Plan 58M-672, at Blair Creek Drive and Blair Valley Street.

debate: On heritage designations, a councillor asked whether owners supported them. Staff said owners are notified by registered letter and only agreed properties come to Council.

On the newcomer strategy, a councillor asked whether other businesses could join the city's internship and mentorship positions. Staff said the first focus is the city's own program but they would look at expanding it.

On the water constraint, a councillor asked about infill applications being deferred and a possible backlog. Staff said they are reviewing applications case by case, over 60 are in progress, and a report back is expected in the coming months.

On the Legacy Walk, councillors asked about overlap with the downtown business association's art walk, timing and budget. Staff said consultation would be part of the work, and funding would come later through a separate budget issue paper. One councillor asked about sponsorship and another about including diverse stories.
On alcohol at park events, the Mayor said the provincial announcement has no legislation yet. Staff will evaluate it, and festivals that rely on food and beverage sales could face financial pressure.
